## Prefer-A draft (Approach A)

**Problem in one line.** Same-PR brief+code is refused because membership reads `file_scope` only from the merge-base brief (#4774 / #5192). That stops a PR from authorizing its own files. The only accepted review proof today is "it merged earlier," which forces a brief-land PR tax (#5949 class; #6198 remint when delivery metadata churns).

**Prefer-A (bind this).** Extend the membership admit path so a forge-attested human approval of the brief's authorization bytes may substitute for prior merge:

1. When the PR adds or widens a brief and changes files inside that brief's `file_scope`, membership MAY evaluate against the **head** brief iff a qualifying forge approval covers the head authorization hash.
2. Authorization hash = `file_scope` + acceptance block only. Exclude delivery metadata such as `plan.metadata.productPullRequest` (kills the #6198 remint class).
3. Qualifying approval: human (not bot), not the PR author, on head SHA or on an earlier SHA whose authorization hash equals head.
4. Any change to authorization fields after approval invalidates the admit.
5. Without a qualifying approval, behavior is unchanged (Path B / merge-base precommitment / mint authority as today).
6. Widen inside the product PR uses the same path under the same approval.
7. `requireHumanMerge` and bot-merge rules stay unchanged.

**Reject B.** Per-PR human policy flag / separate Path-C verb — adds ceremony without binding the forge attestation to authorization bytes.

**Reject C.** In-tree approved-scope / mint twin written in the same PR — agent-writable; same-PR rewrite already hard-fails for that reason (#3145 / #3205). Body already rejects this.

**Keep-outs.** Do not weaken mint authority when a continuity mint is present (#5192). Do not auto-merge. Do not treat bot or author self-approve as qualifying. Residual: hosts where the agent holds a second human token (state posture; not solved by hash alone).

**Related.** #5949 becomes a subset; #6197 / #5973 widen exemptions and #6199 mint handoff become moot under the general rule; #6198 remint class retires when PPR is outside the hash.

**KISS.** Bound limbs stay short mechanism only. Docs/naming/alias are footnotes (#5783 / #3265 / #3368).

## Verdict

Prefer-A survives the refutation charter as a mechanism, but cannot bind as written. Prior merge is not logically necessary: a separately trusted forge approval can authorize a precisely identified scope without that scope having merged first. The draft needs the authority-selection and proof-binding rules below before pain-audit. This is not a finding that P1 is solved.

## Pin-read verification

Read the issue body, Prefer-A [6811297341](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6203#issuecomment-6811297341), Stop 1 [6811305107](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6203#issuecomment-6811305107), and deposit [6811324579](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/6203#issuecomment-6811324579), without reading sibling posts or later comments. Deposit ceiling matches the envelope; panel completeness is not observable by this seat.

Used `git show e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a:packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts` and the pinned design-critique contract. This is source inspection, not executed integration tests or verification of live GitHub review semantics.

Existing mechanisms: `evaluateApprovedScopeMembership` distinguishes mint, concrete precommitment, and missing authority; an empty mint remains authoritative; missing own scope cannot be rescued by peer coverage; test/fixture extras do not receive production allowance. `evaluateProductionScopeFence` independently retains a merge-base scope and capped allowance. The membership evaluator accepts caller-supplied authority and scope; it does not authenticate forge reviews. These are real boundaries the new proof resolver must preserve, not proof that prior merge is the only possible authorization mechanism.

## F1 — blocks-the-design: mint precedence must be in the admit predicate (P4)

Evidence: Prefer-A limb 1 permits head scope whenever approval qualifies; its keep-out separately forbids weakening a continuity mint. The pinned evaluator treats even an empty mint as authoritative and explicitly says widening the brief cannot clear a mint refusal.

Failure: a qualifying approval plus widened head scope could replace an existing restrictive or empty mint if limb 1 is implemented literally. A successful new proof would then weaken authority even though the no-approval fallback is correct.

Required disposition: make existing continuity-mint authority take precedence over the new path. Only without a present mint may qualifying forge proof select head scope; otherwise use today's mint/precommitment/missing behavior and remediation. Invalid or unavailable proof must not turn into an empty-success result. Accept the fallback goal, block its currently incomplete precedence.

## F2 — blocks-the-design: approval needs authorization, current validity, and immutable context (P3)

Evidence: Prefer-A limb 3 says only human, non-author, and matching SHA/hash. It does not require repository authority to approve scope, exclude withdrawn/dismissed approval, or bind the hash to one repository/PR/story. The pinned evaluator cannot supply those checks.

Failure: those predicates alone admit a different human account without scope-approval authority; an adapter could also reuse a historical approval after withdrawal or reuse equal field bytes for another brief. Concurrent pushes can detach a fetched review/hash pair from the head actually being gated.

Required disposition: resolve a currently effective approval from an authorized non-author human on this repository/PR, bind it to the same continuity-resolved story and reviewed commit, and verify against the immutable candidate head being gated. Unknown identity/authority, unavailable reviewed bytes, withdrawn approval, or candidate mismatch selects fallback. Scope approval carried forward by hash does not replace whatever code-review/merge controls independently require.

## F3 — blocks-the-design: define the hashed projection without hiding authorization inputs (P2)

Evidence: limb 2 names an 'acceptance block' without a schema selector; the evaluator separately consumes plan identity, lifecycle exemptions, peer scopes, and path-classification inputs in addition to file scope.

Failure: excluding delivery metadata is correct, but treating all metadata as irrelevant can allow a changed authority selector to retain an old approval. Conversely, serializing the whole brief recreates the PPR remint problem. This is a projection-definition gap, not evidence that every evaluator input belongs in the hash.

Required disposition: specify a deterministic schema-versioned projection of file scope and the exact acceptance fields, with repository/PR/story identity separately bound to the proof. Every omitted input that can alter membership authority must retain an independently trusted source; omission cannot authorize its same-PR replacement. Delivery-only PPR stamping must leave the projection unchanged. Compare the same projection of reviewed-commit and candidate-head bytes.

## F4 — sharpens-framing: independent credentials remain a deployment assumption (P1)

Evidence: both the issue and Prefer-A explicitly admit an agent-held second human token. The proposed checks observe account identity, not who controls its credentials.

Failure: an agent controlling an otherwise authorized second account can satisfy all forge predicates itself. Hashing prevents subsequent scope drift; it cannot establish independent human intent.

Disposition: retain this as an explicit unresolved trust assumption, not claimed relief. On hosts without approval-credential separation, the new path cannot provide the advertised independent-human guarantee. A documentation statement alone does not close that residual. This narrows the security claim while preserving the mechanism for deployments with that separation.

## F5 — sharpens-framing: membership success is narrower than one-PR success

Evidence: the same pinned file contains a separate production fence whose base scope is explicitly never head, with a 2–5 file allowance. Prefer-A only changes membership.

Failure: a new brief plus a larger production change can pass the new membership path and still exceed that independent fence. Therefore claims that the general rule retires all brief-land/widen cases are not established by this design. Caller integration was outside this envelope and was not verified.

Disposition: keep the production fence unchanged and qualify the ceremony-reduction claim; if overriding that fence is intended, that is another authority change needing an explicit decision. Do not quietly route head scope into both evaluators.

## Short mechanism changes before pain-audit

- Preserve mint precedence; otherwise select authenticated head scope or today's fallback.
- Bind a currently valid, authorized independent review to repository/PR/story and immutable reviewed/candidate commits.
- Compare one defined authorization projection; keep omitted authority inputs independently trusted and PPR-only edits neutral.

P1 remains a stated trust limitation; F5 bounds the benefit claim. Neither needs another gate or a long Bound-remedy limb.

Road not taken: retain prior merge as the sole path. Its strongest case is avoiding a second approval resolver and its trust surface. It wins if the forge adapter cannot reliably establish authorization and current review validity; otherwise the additional resolver is sufficient to refute the sole-path premise without introducing agent-writable approval records.

At dispatch-sha `e514bc81132ff8c3bfbb5f9cdf6490d80bfcdc5a` (dest HEAD matches):

- `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/base-fence.ts`: `evaluateApprovedScopeMembership` admits only via `baseApprovedFileScope` under `mint | precommitment | missing`. Present mint is authoritative (including empty).
- `evaluateProductionScopeFence`: `baseFileScope` only; comment "Does not read the head brief"; over-budget detail "head brief edits do not widen the fence (#4956)". Empty base scope → no production-fence finding.

Stop 1 anchors (prior-merge-only membership proof; P1–P4) match this pin surface. Launch-probe is not method verification.

## Verdict on Prefer-A vs refutation charter

**Prefer-A survives the refutation charter conditionally.** The sole-path presumption ("prior merge is the only forge-attested proof that may authorize membership against that brief's `file_scope`") is refutable for the Path B / missing-precommitment tax class the issue measures: a forge-attested non-author human APPROVED review bound to an authorization-field hash is a second forge-attested proof class outside the agent data plane. Prefer-A as written does **not** yet bind tightly enough to mint interaction, hash schema, approver predicates, or production-fence widen — those Bound-limb sharpenings must land before pain-audit. P1 remains leftover residual (named, unsolved by hash).

Injection / swarm lens: fires (membership authority + forge identity + PR tip state).

## Findings

### F1 — Mint-present override hole — `sharpens-framing`

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A limb 1 says membership MAY evaluate against the **head** brief under qualifying forge approval. Prefer-A Keep-outs say "Do not weaken mint authority when a continuity mint is present (#5192)." Pin-read: present mint is authoritative; widening merge-base brief / Live HEAD cannot clear mint outside. Limb list does not encode the mint conjunct; keep-out prose is not a Bound mechanism under Thin Fail-Closed (#3265).
- **Failure mode:** Forge-approved head brief admits paths a present (including empty) mint refuses → Prefer-A silently demotes mint from membership SoT to advisory, recreating same-PR self-auth against the stronger authority class.
- **Disposition:** Fold into Bound: forge-approval head-brief admit is lawful **only** when `allowlistAuthority` is `precommitment` or `missing`. Present mint → today's mint path unchanged; forge approval does not substitute.

### F2 — Widen claim vs production fence — `sharpens-framing`

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A limb 6: widen inside product PR under same approval. Pin-read production fence never reads head and refuses production extras past allowance (2–5) with "head brief edits do not widen." Issue acceptance names membership only.
- **Failure mode:** Membership admits under forge approval while production fence still refuses over-allowance widen → Prefer-A's "one PR" / widen tax removal is incomplete or silently dual-gated.
- **Disposition:** Bound must pick one short mechanism: (a) same auth-hash forge admit also feeds production-fence allowlist for that story, or (b) Prefer-A is membership-only and widen-over-allowance stays split / brief-land. Do not leave both gates implied.

### F3 — Authorization-hash field set underspecified — `sharpens-framing` (P2)

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A hashes "`file_scope` + acceptance block" and excludes delivery metadata (e.g. `productPullRequest`). Pin has no closed "acceptance block" field set for this hash. Identity binding (`plan.id`, `xbriefRelPath` / continuity key) is unnamed.
- **Failure mode:** Including delivery metadata recreates #6198 remint (P2 left). Excluding `file_scope` or acceptance opens self-auth (P2 right). Omitting story identity lets a same-PR sibling brief's approval cover the wrong allowlist. Ambiguous "acceptance block" makes hash drift non-deterministic across implementers.
- **Disposition:** Bound pins a closed canonical byte set (ordered concrete paths + named acceptance fields + continuity identity keys). Explicit exclude list for delivery metadata. Any auth-field change after approval drops head admit (already Prefer-A limb 4 — keep).

### F4 — Approver / SHA predicates underspecified — `sharpens-framing` (P3)

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A: "human (not bot), not the PR author, on head SHA or earlier SHA whose authorization hash equals head." Pin has no forge-review helper in `base-fence.ts`; human-origin grants (`content/contracts/human-origin-authz.md`) reject agent-lifecycle / self-asserted origins but do not define GitHub review USER vs BOT.
- **Failure mode:** Bot APPROVED, author self-APPROVED, COMMENT-as-LGTM, or auth-hash drift after approval still head-admits → P3 open. "Human" without closed predicate (e.g. GitHub `user.type == User`, not App/Bot) is rubber language. Earlier-SHA path without requiring the approved commit's tree to carry the hashed auth bytes invites tip rewrite races.
- **Disposition:** Bound closed predicates: review state `APPROVED` only; reviewer login ≠ PR `.user.login`; reviewer not Bot/App; approved commit is head or ancestor whose extracted auth-hash equals head; mismatch → Path B remediation (P4). ⊗ Reviewer-attention as the control.

### F5 — Confused-deputy residual must be leftover-pain, not buried keep-out — `sharpens-framing` (P1)

- **Evidence:** Body and Prefer-A name hosts where the agent holds a second human forge token as residual ("state posture; not solved by hash alone"). Injection lens applies. Contract forbids closing a safety case on reviewer attention without a deterministic control.
- **Failure mode:** Agent-orchestrated second-account APPROVED review looks qualifying; Prefer-A's core substitute for prior merge is agent-controllable on those hosts → confused-deputy bypass of the membership fence.
- **Disposition:** Prefer-A may bind under open materiality with P1 cited as leftover-pain / deferred control (host posture, org ruleset, or future attestation that the reviewing identity is outside agent credential plane). Do not claim P1 closed by hash. Do not leave it only as Keep-outs prose without a bind-lean pain cite.

### F6 — Missing/invalid approval keeps Path B — `footnote` (P4 accept)

- **Evidence:** Prefer-A limb 5: without qualifying approval, behavior unchanged (Path B / merge-base / mint). Pin-read already fail-closes missing declaration and outside-allowlist with split-or-land remediation.
- **Failure mode:** Only if implement wires head-brief as default when approval probe errors soft — that would be a later implement defect, not Prefer-A as written.
- **Disposition:** Keep opt-in admit; approval probe failure / invalid → today's Path B. No Bound remint for P4 unless wiring softens.

## Bound limbs that must land before pain-audit

1. Forge head-brief membership admit **only** when mint authority is absent (`precommitment` | `missing`).
2. Closed auth-hash byte set (identity + `file_scope` + acceptance fields; delivery metadata out).
3. Closed approver/SHA predicates (APPROVED; non-author; non-bot; hash-equal SHA binding).
4. Production-fence interaction chosen: share forge admit, or membership-only with narrowed widen claim.
5. P1 recorded leftover-pain / deferred control on the bind lean.

## Road-not-taken / steelman

- **Road not taken:** Keep prior-merge-only and only streamline brief-land handoff (#6199). Rejected: does not remove the measured 3-PR / lifecycle-JSON tax.
- **Steelman of refutation-target:** Prior merge is durable default-branch attestation; PR-tip APPROVED is ephemeral and requestable by an agent. **Flip:** Bound limbs 1–4 plus an explicit P1 leftover (or host control) — then the sole-path claim fails for the adoption-blocker tax class without pretending confused-deputy is solved.

metadata.issueBody:
## Problem

A code change costs at least three PRs: land the brief, land the code, land the completion. A consumer run on 0.129.6 shipped 6 product PRs inside 22 total. Lifecycle PRs added about 8,100 lines of JSON against about 8,400 product lines. A 14-line hook refresh took 3 PRs. A Directive upgrade took 4, one only to add two ignore paths to the brief's `file_scope`.

The brief-first PR is required by design. `verify:scope-provenance` reads `file_scope` only from the merge-base brief (#4774 / #5192), so a PR that carries a new brief plus its code is refused. That rule stops a PR from authorising its own files. It is correct. But the only accepted proof of review today is "it merged earlier". A human approval of the brief inside the same PR would prove the same thing.

## Proposal

Admit a brief and its implementation in one PR when a forge-attested human approval covers the brief bytes:

1. The PR adds or widens a brief and changes files inside that brief's `file_scope`.
2. A human who is not the PR author approves the PR on the head SHA, or on an earlier SHA whose authorization fields hash the same as head.
3. The merge gate checks: approval exists, approver is human and not the author, and the head authorization hash equals the approved hash. Any change to the authorization fields after approval invalidates it.

**What the hash covers.** Hash the authorization fields only: `file_scope` and the acceptance block. Leave out delivery metadata such as `plan.metadata.productPullRequest`. A whole-brief hash would drop the approval every time the product PR number is stamped, which brings back the #6198 remint class.
4. With that proof, membership evaluates against the head brief instead of the merge-base brief.

Widen uses the same path: a widened `file_scope` in the product PR is admitted under the same approval, so no separate widen PR.

Without a qualifying approval, behaviour is unchanged (Path B brief-land first).

## Why a forge approval, not an in-tree record

An in-tree record (approved-scope file, mint) is bytes an agent can write. Same-PR rewrite of those records already hard-fails for that reason. A GitHub review by a different human account, bound to a commit SHA, is outside the agent's data plane. Hosts where the agent holds a second human token are the residual risk and need a stated posture.

## Acceptance

- One PR carrying a new brief plus code inside its `file_scope` passes membership when the approval rule holds, and fails with today's remediation when it does not.
- Changing `file_scope` or acceptance after approval drops the admit.
- Stamping `productPullRequest` (or other delivery metadata) after approval keeps the admit.
- Widen inside a product PR is admitted under the same approval.
- `requireHumanMerge` and bot-merge rules are unchanged.

## Related

- #5949 asks for this for human-approved chore/deposit check-ins only. This issue is the general case; #5949 becomes a subset.
- #6198 (PPR remint), #6197 / #5973 (single-path widen exemptions) are instances a general rule would retire.
- #5192 / #4774 / #4956 rationale for the merge-base fence.
- #6199 (agent lands mint twins after a human mint) becomes moot: there is no separate brief-land PR to hand off.
- #3813 ceremony economy: this removes a refusal round-trip; it adds no new fail-closed gate.

Mechanism-shaped: run design-critique before implementation.
